name: pixelated-canvas
title: Pixelated Canvas
description: Turns a photograph into a dotted, halftone-like picture on a dark canvas. Moving the pointer swirls the dots near it while the rest keeps still, then the image settles back.
use: A hero or portfolio image should feel tactile and respond to the visitor without any click.
avoid: The canvas keeps a fixed pixel size, so it will not stretch to a fluid column, and very dark photos look full of holes.
a11y: The canvas has an aria-label and image role, but the distortion is pointer-only and there is no reduced-motion check. (keyboard: no, labels: good, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A rectangular canvas filled with thousands of small coloured dots that together form a mountain and sky photo: teal-blue slopes below, warm orange horizon above. Dots thin out in low-contrast areas, leaving dark gaps, and a small grey caption sits under the canvas.
behaves: Pointer movement pushes the dots near the cursor into a swirl that fades with distance. When the pointer leaves, the motion eases out and the dots drift back to their original positions, leaving a still dotted image.
customise: The image source, canvas size, dot size and shape, distortion mode and strength, tint and grayscale are all props; sampling logic needs a source edit.
weight: heavy: A full canvas redraws every dot on each animation frame, continuously while mounted.
demo: A dotted mountain-at-dusk photo captioned "Move cursor over the canvas to distort".
issues: Dots disappear in dark, low-contrast regions, leaving visible holes in the picture.
The canvas uses a fixed pixel width and height, so it will not refill a resized column.
polishWhy: Distinctive dot rendering and a convincing swirl; the dropout gaps and fixed size hold it back.
